talent: The boy's talent for drawing horses made everyone smile.
Do you think you have a talent for baking cakes?
Winning the school talent show was the best day ever!
silent: Please stay silent while the others finish the test.
The cat crept across the lawn, silent as a shadow.
Why is the classroom so silent today?
parent: Ask a parent to sign the form and bring it back.
Every parent was invited to the school concert on Friday.
Which parent will help us bake the cakes?
urgent: Is it urgent, or can the homework wait until tomorrow?
I must post this letter today because it is urgent.
The plumber came at once because the leak was urgent.
silence: The room fell into silence when the music stopped.
Can we have some silence while I read my book?
The clock ticked loudly in the silence of the library.
absence: Please bring a note to explain your absence from school.
In the absence of the teacher, a helper read us a story.
During my absence on holiday, the plants grew very tall.
difference: What is the difference between a rabbit and a hare?
The difference between nine and four is five.
A little paint made a big difference to the old chair.
evidence: The empty plate was evidence that someone had eaten the last biscuit.
Our experiment gave us evidence that warm water melts ice faster.
What evidence do you have that the dog dug the hole?
urgency: With great urgency, we ran to bring the washing in before the rain.
Why is there such urgency to finish the model today?
Nobody saw the urgency of getting the tent up before dark.
frequency: The bus runs with a frequency of one every ten minutes.
We counted the frequency of red cars passing the school gate.
We made a chart of the frequency of rainy days in May.

rejected.s: A parent duck led her ducklings across the pond.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Parent duck' is awkward; a child would expect 'mother duck'.

rejected.s: What a lovely cake my parent made for my birthday!
rejected.reason: checker: 'My parent' is unnatural in everyday British English.

rejected.s: After the loud party, the quiet house felt full of silence.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Full of silence' after 'quiet' is awkward and says the same thing twice.

rejected.s: Dinner was ready, but we noticed the cat's absence.
rejected.reason: checker: 'We noticed the cat's silence' also makes sense. (also fits: silence)

rejected.s: The bus was leaving, so she ran with real urgency.
rejected.reason: checker: Running to catch a bus is a road setting, so it is dropped to be safe.
